messages:
alex: Morning team — async standup: API gateway / routing / auth / rate limits

alex: What I did: pushed a small routing rule cleanup for the ingress-lane PR, added a fallback to the jwt-auth middleware so expired tokens return 401 earlier. Opened PR #1287. Ran canary against staging. :white_check_mark:

alex: Blockers: noticed an odd spike of 429s during the canary for a subset of internal health pings, looks like ratepolicy merge logic double-counting some prefix matches. Haven't traced root cause yet.

marina: Nice. Re: 429s — I saw similar in prod last week; it came down to overlapping route tags in the ratepolicy cache. Do you have a quick example of the rules that collided?

alex: Yep — snippet below from the live policy that triggered it:

```
- id: team-internal
  prefix: /api/internal
  keys: [service, client_id]
  limit: 120/s
- id: infra-health
  prefix: /api/internal/health
  keys: [service]
  limit: 60/s
```

alex: The runtime was counting both prefixes for /api/internal/health because of our prefix lookup order when a request matched multiple policies.

jason: Oof. I can pair on this — sounds like the route-matcher doesn't short-circuit when it finds an exact longer prefix. I can reproduce locally if you drop the policy YAML and a sample request.

alex: Thanks — dropping the YAML in thread: attaching in a follow-up comment. For now I flipped a temp patch that evaluates longest-prefix-first before aggregating limits; staging canary looks cleaner but we need tests.

sylvia: For rollout: suggest canary 10% for 30 min, then 50% for 1h, keep automatic rollback if 5xx > 0.5% or 429 rate increases by >30% vs baseline. Agree?

marina: Sounds good. Also add a metric for "ratepolicy_overlap_count" so we can alert when multiple policies match the same request — that would've caught this earlier.

alex: Good call. I'll add the metric alongside the patch.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-ingress-v2 -> staging (tag: canary-3895). Logs: https://ci.example/redwood/3895

rui: Quick FYI — jwt rotation that alex mentioned: I rotated keys in staging last night, and a few clients that reuse long-lived tokens hit auth errors; I rolled forward a grace window in the middleware to smooth it. We'll still need a follow-up to harden rotation flow.

alex: Thanks @rui. Today: write unit+integration tests for prefix ordering, add the overlap metric, and open a small RFC for route matching precedence so it's documented. If anyone can review PR #1287 and the test PR today that would help move the canary to prod tomorrow.

jason: Happy to review this afternoon — ping me when PR is ready.

marina: I'll do a pass on the telemetry bits and the alert thresholds.

sylvia: I'll schedule the rollout window in the ops calendar and set the pager for the first 30m.

alex: Cool — thanks all. If anything urgent, ping me @alex or drop in #eng-oncall.

alex: (small note) I added a quick smokecheck script: `scripts/smoke_route_overlap.sh` — runs a burst against /api/internal/health and validates single-policy attribution. Use in staging after deploy.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: canary-ingress-v2 -> staging (success).

alex: Last msg — will mark this done once tests + metric PRs merged.
